BackstoryDef.title: rebel prince
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up a prince without a kingdom, watching [PAWN_possessive] mother hand the county to foreign nobles. Still a boy, [PAWN_pronoun] knighted [PAWN_objective]self in a cathedral and swore to take back what was [PAWN_possessive].

BackstoryDef.description: The son of the governor of Sines, a small fishing town on the Alentejo coast, [PAWN_nameDef] grew up watching ships come and go. [PAWN_nameDef] learned mathematics and navigation and dreamed of what lay beyond the horizon.

A stern and sometimes brutal captain, [PAWN_pronoun] held [PAWN_possessive] crews together through storms, scurvy and near-mutiny.

BackstoryDef.description: Against all advice, [PAWN_nameDef] led the flower of Portugal's nobility on a crusade into Morocco and vanished at the battle of Alcácer Quibir. With no heir, Portugal fell to Spain, and for centuries the people waited for their king to ride back out of the fog one morning.\n\nIt seems [PAWN_pronoun] finally has.

BackstoryDef.description: In June 1940, with refugees fleeing the Nazi advance crowding the streets of Bordeaux, consul [PAWN_nameDef] defied direct orders and signed visas day and night for anyone who asked. BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Castelo de Vide, a hilltop town near the Spanish border, where [PAWN_pronoun] spent more time with horses than with schoolbooks.

BackstoryDef.description: On 25 April 1974, cavalry captain [PAWN_nameDef] led a column of armoured cars from Santarém into Lisbon and, without firing a shot, forced the head of the dictatorship to surrender. BackstoryDef.description: Raised by [PAWN_possessive] grandmother in a poor Lisbon household, [PAWN_nameDef] sold fruit on the city docks and sang to draw in customers. Passers-by stopped more often to listen than to buy.

Dressed in black with eyes closed, [PAWN_pronoun] sang of longing and fate so powerfully that audiences who understood not a word wept anyway. BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Amadora, on the outskirts of Lisbon, where the only thing [PAWN_pronoun] cared about more than football was talking about football.

BackstoryDef.description: After a modest playing career, [PAWN_nameDef] became one of the most successful coaches in Portuguese football, winning titles with Benfica before conquering South America with Flamengo. BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up by the sea in Porto, running everywhere instead of walking. The local boys could rarely keep up with [PAWN_objective].

BackstoryDef.description: Small, slight and seemingly tireless, [PAWN_nameDef] became the best marathon runner in the world: three times European champion, world champion, and the first Portuguese woman to win Olympic gold, in Seoul in 1988.

BackstoryDef.title: coffee king
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] founded Delta Cafés and built it into Portugal's best-known coffee brand, without ever leaving [PAWN_possessive] small Alentejo town. [PAWN_pronoun] knew [PAWN_possessive] workers by name and spent a fortune on [PAWN_possessive] community, and the whole country called [PAWN_objective] simply "o Comendador".

BackstoryDef.title: mine helper
BackstoryDef.description: Born into a humble family in a village near Viseu, [PAWN_nameDef] went to work very young as a helper at a mine, and spent [PAWN_possessive] free time chasing a football around the local pitch.

BackstoryDef.title: marathon gold medallist
BackstoryDef.description: Two weeks before the 1984 Olympics, [PAWN_nameDef] was knocked down by a car while training in Lisbon. [PAWN_pronoun] ran the Los Angeles marathon anyway, won it at 37 with an Olympic record that stood for 24 years, and gave Portugal its first ever Olympic gold medal.

BackstoryDef.title: too-fast girl
BackstoryDef.description: As a girl in Penafiel, [PAWN_nameDef] beat runners much older than [PAWN_objective], so easily that some organisers refused to believe a child could really have won.

BackstoryDef.title: Olympic champion
BackstoryDef.description: In the 10,000 metres final at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics, [PAWN_nameDef] was ten metres behind the world record holder with the finish in sight. [PAWN_pronoun] reeled her in, won gold with an Olympic record, and became one of Portugal's greatest athletes.

BackstoryDef.title: hyperactive river kid
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was such a hyperactive child in Ponte de Lima that someone suggested putting [PAWN_objective] in a kayak on the river Lima to burn off the energy. [PAWN_pronoun] never got out again.

BackstoryDef.title: kayak champion
BackstoryDef.description: With two Olympic medals, several world titles and well over a hundred international medals, [PAWN_nameDef] is the most decorated paddler in Portuguese history. [PAWN_pronoun] calls the calluses on [PAWN_possessive] hands "invisible medals".

BackstoryDef.title: minibike racer
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was racing minibikes around Almada almost as soon as [PAWN_possessive] feet could reach the pegs, and spent the rest of [PAWN_possessive] time in the garage with greasy hands.

BackstoryDef.title: MotoGP winner
BackstoryDef.description: "The Falcon of Almada" became the first Portuguese rider to win a MotoGP race, snatching [PAWN_possessive] first victory at the very last corner. [PAWN_nameDef] later won [PAWN_possessive] home Grand Prix in Portimão from pole position, leading every single lap.

BackstoryDef.title: girl of the sea
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in an old Porto family, spending long summers on the beach at Granja, where the sea, the light and the gardens of [PAWN_possessive] childhood became the stuff of [PAWN_possessive] poems.

BackstoryDef.title: poet of the sea
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] became one of Portugal's greatest poets and won the Camões Prize. [PAWN_possessive] children's stories, like "The Girl from the Sea", are read in every Portuguese school, and [PAWN_possessive] poem greeting 25 April 1974 as "the dawn I was waiting for" is part of the revolution's memory.

BackstoryDef.title: stargazer
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Lisbon fascinated by maps and stars, and joined the navy to see the places on them for [PAWN_objective]self.

BackstoryDef.title: air navigator
BackstoryDef.description: Naval officer and mapmaker [PAWN_nameDef] invented a sextant that could be used from the air. In 1922 [PAWN_pronoun] used it to navigate the first flight across the South Atlantic, from Lisbon to Rio de Janeiro, finding tiny islands in the middle of the ocean with nothing but the sun and the stars.

BackstoryDef.title: daredevil
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was the boy who climbed the highest trees and jumped off the highest walls. When aeroplanes were invented, it was obvious where [PAWN_pronoun] would end up.

BackstoryDef.title: aviation pioneer
BackstoryDef.description: Naval aviator [PAWN_nameDef] piloted the seaplane on the first flight across the South Atlantic in 1922, with Gago Coutinho navigating. They wrecked two planes on the way and finished in a third, and were greeted in Rio de Janeiro as heroes.

BackstoryDef.title: prince of Porto
BackstoryDef.description: Born in Porto, the son of King João I and Philippa of Lancaster, [PAWN_nameDef] grew up at court with [PAWN_possessive] brothers, raised on chivalry, mathematics and tales of lands beyond the known world.

BackstoryDef.title: patron of discovery
BackstoryDef.description: Known as Henry the Navigator, [PAWN_nameDef] barely sailed [PAWN_objective]self. Instead [PAWN_pronoun] gathered pilots, mapmakers and shipbuilders, and sent expedition after expedition down the coast of Africa, starting the Age of Discovery.

BackstoryDef.title: court page
BackstoryDef.description: Born to a minor noble family in the north of Portugal, [PAWN_nameDef] served as a page at the royal court in Lisbon, where the talk was all of spices, ships and the Indies.

BackstoryDef.title: circumnavigator
BackstoryDef.description: Snubbed by the Portuguese king, [PAWN_nameDef] sailed for Spain instead and led the first expedition around the world. [PAWN_pronoun] found the strait at the tip of South America that still bears [PAWN_possessive] name and crossed the Pacific, but was killed in battle in the Philippines before the voyage ended.

BackstoryDef.title: ambitious squire
BackstoryDef.description: Born into minor Lisbon gentry, [PAWN_nameDef] grew up with more ambition than money, studying law and history and waiting for [PAWN_possessive] chance.

BackstoryDef.title: iron-fisted minister
BackstoryDef.description: When the great earthquake of 1755 destroyed Lisbon, chief minister [PAWN_nameDef] took charge: bury the dead, feed the living, rebuild. [PAWN_pronoun] raised a new city of straight streets and earthquake-proof buildings, and ruled the country with an iron fist for over twenty years.

BackstoryDef.title: Galician noblewoman
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was born into one of the most powerful noble families of Galicia, and came to Portugal as a lady-in-waiting to the bride of the heir to the throne.

BackstoryDef.title: queen after death
BackstoryDef.description: Prince Pedro fell hopelessly in love with [PAWN_nameDef] instead of his wife, and the king, fearing her family's influence, had her killed in Coimbra. When Pedro became king, he hunted down her murderers, and legend says he had her body crowned and the whole court kiss her hand: the queen who was crowned after her death.

BackstoryDef.title: princess of Aragon
BackstoryDef.description: A princess of Aragon, [PAWN_nameDef] was married off to King Dinis of Portugal at twelve. Even as a girl, [PAWN_pronoun] was known for giving away whatever [PAWN_pronoun] had to the poor.

BackstoryDef.title: saint queen
BackstoryDef.description: Queen [PAWN_nameDef] founded hospitals, fed the hungry and twice rode between armies to stop her husband and son from going to war. Legend says the king once caught her carrying bread to the poor in her lap, but when she opened it, the bread had turned into roses.

BackstoryDef.title: Minho farm girl
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up working the fields around Póvoa de Lanhoso, in the green hills of the Minho, where people were poor, devout and quick to anger.

BackstoryDef.title: leader of the revolt
BackstoryDef.description: In 1846, when the government banned burials inside churches and raised taxes, the women of the Minho rose up, armed with pitchforks and sickles. Their leader, remembered as [PAWN_nameDef] though nobody is sure who she really was, started a revolt that spread across the country and brought down the government.

BackstoryDef.title: girl who wanted more
BackstoryDef.description: Growing up in Guarda, [PAWN_nameDef] decided early that she would study medicine, at a time when almost no women in Portugal went to university.

BackstoryDef.title: pioneer surgeon
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was the first woman to perform surgery in a Portuguese hospital. In 1911 she noticed the electoral law only required voters to be literate heads of family, and as a widow with a daughter, she was one. She took her case to court, won, and became the first woman ever to vote in Portugal. The law was quickly changed to stop anyone following her.

BackstoryDef.title: Setúbal rhymer
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was writing verses in Setúbal before most children could write their names, and already used them to mock anyone who annoyed [PAWN_objective].

BackstoryDef.title: bohemian poet
BackstoryDef.description: After deserting the navy in India, [PAWN_nameDef] came back to Lisbon and became the most brilliant and the most scandalous poet of [PAWN_possessive] age. [PAWN_possessive] satire landed [PAWN_objective] in the prisons of the Inquisition, and two centuries later every dirty joke in Portugal is still told about "Bocage".

BackstoryDef.title: bookish boy
BackstoryDef.description: Born in Póvoa de Varzim and raised mostly by [PAWN_possessive] grandparents, [PAWN_nameDef] found [PAWN_possessive] company in books, and later in the student circles of Coimbra.

BackstoryDef.title: novelist and consul
BackstoryDef.description: While serving as a consul in Havana, England and Paris, [PAWN_nameDef] wrote novels that mercilessly mocked the hypocrisy of Portuguese society. "The Maias" is still considered the great Portuguese novel, and [PAWN_possessive] remains now rest in the National Pantheon.

BackstoryDef.title: Rans village boy
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Rans, a village in Penafiel, and started working young, learning to lay Portugal's traditional cobblestone pavements one stone at a time.

BackstoryDef.title: people's candidate
BackstoryDef.description: Cobblestone paver, parish council president, singer of "Pão, Pão, Fiambre, Fiambre", reality show contestant and candidate for President of the Republic more than once: [PAWN_nameDef] has done it all with the same unshakeable optimism, and a paver's hammer never far away.

BackstoryDef.title: Gaia kid
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up poor in Vila Nova de Gaia with four siblings, and found the great love of [PAWN_possessive] life early: FC Porto.

BackstoryDef.title: legendary photobomber
BackstoryDef.description: For more than thirty years, whenever a TV crew went live anywhere near Porto, [PAWN_nameDef] somehow appeared right behind the reporter, smiling at the camera. Between broadcasts [PAWN_pronoun] worked for fifteen years at a bakery. Reporters joke that a big story in Porto isn't official until the Emplastro shows up.

BackstoryDef.title: bedroom dancer
BackstoryDef.description: Growing up between Lisbon and Cacém, [PAWN_nameDef] taught [PAWN_objective]self to dance in front of the mirror and made strange songs nobody else would have dared to make.

BackstoryDef.title: Eurovision oddity
BackstoryDef.description: After studying graphic design and spending years working in a Lisbon sex shop, [PAWN_nameDef] won the Portuguese Eurovision selection with "Telemóveis", a song about smashing your phone, sung half like fado and half like nothing anyone had ever heard. It didn't reach the final, but the country never forgot it.

BackstoryDef.title: Galician runaway
BackstoryDef.description: Born into a poor village in Galicia, [PAWN_nameDef] left home young and came to Lisbon looking for work, like thousands of Galicians of [PAWN_possessive] time.

BackstoryDef.title: aqueduct killer
BackstoryDef.description: In the 1830s, legend says, [PAWN_nameDef] waited on Lisbon's great aqueduct, robbing passers-by and throwing them off into the valley below; the deaths were at first taken for suicides. [PAWN_pronoun] was hanged in 1841, and [PAWN_possessive] head, preserved in a jar, is still kept at Lisbon's faculty of medicine.

BackstoryDef.title: girl of mysteries
BackstoryDef.description: Growing up in Amadora, [PAWN_nameDef] was fascinated by horoscopes, cards and anything mysterious, and loved nothing more than an audience.

BackstoryDef.title: TV tarot reader
BackstoryDef.description: Primary school teacher, revue actress, circus artist, newspaper astrologer: [PAWN_nameDef] tried it all before becoming the country's best-known tarot reader, predicting the year ahead for the whole nation on television and hosting shows from breakfast time to well past midnight.

BackstoryDef.title: singer's daughter
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was singing on stage with [PAWN_possessive] father, a popular singer, from the age of six, and was hosting a children's TV show by fifteen.

BackstoryDef.title: pop turbo queen
BackstoryDef.description: Mixing pop, pimba and reggaeton, [PAWN_nameDef] became the best-selling pop artist in Portugal. Nobody sells a song, or a nickname like "Turbinada", with more energy.

BackstoryDef.title: worried child
BackstoryDef.description: Even as a boy in Restelo, [PAWN_nameDef] warned the other children that climbing trees would end in tragedy. It usually did, and [PAWN_pronoun] never let them forget it.

BackstoryDef.title: prophet of doom
BackstoryDef.description: As Vasco da Gama's fleet set sail for India in 1497, a venerable old man stood on the beach of Restelo and loudly cursed the vain greed for glory that would drown them all. Camões immortalised [PAWN_possessive] speech in "Os Lusíadas", and ever since, every Portuguese naysayer has been called a "Velho do Restelo". [PAWN_pronoun] is still certain it will all end badly.

BackstoryDef.title: Coimbra creature
BackstoryDef.description: Nobody is quite sure what [PAWN_nameDef] is: something between a bear and a dog, born in Coimbra with Brazilian roots. [PAWN_pronoun] spent [PAWN_possessive] childhood having strong opinions about everything and doing nothing about any of them.

BackstoryDef.title: armchair philosopher
BackstoryDef.description: After basic training at the special operations school in Lamego, [PAWN_nameDef] settled into a life of endless, absurd conversations with [PAWN_possessive] friends: a talking bust of Napoleon and a prehistoric man from the Buçaco forest who needs subtitles. [PAWN_pronoun] has advice for everyone, and none of it is good.

BackstoryDef.title: pious princess
BackstoryDef.description: The eldest daughter of the king, [PAWN_nameDef] grew up at a court still shaken by the great earthquake of 1755, more at home in chapel than at feasts.

BackstoryDef.title: mad queen
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] became Portugal's first reigning queen, but after losing her husband, her eldest son and her confessor in a few short years, she sank into a melancholy madness and her son had to rule in her place. When Napoleon invaded and the court fled to Brazil, legend has her telling the coachmen: "Don't go so fast, they'll think we're running away!"

BackstoryDef.title: spare prince
BackstoryDef.description: As a younger son, [PAWN_nameDef] was never meant to rule, and spent [PAWN_possessive] childhood quietly, enjoying music, church ceremonies and, above all, dinner.

BackstoryDef.title: runaway king
BackstoryDef.description: When Napoleon's army marched on Lisbon, [PAWN_nameDef] packed up the entire court, some fifteen thousand people, and sailed for Brazil, ruling the empire from Rio de Janeiro for thirteen years. Popular legend says [PAWN_pronoun] always carried roast chicken in [PAWN_possessive] coat pockets, just in case.

BackstoryDef.title: wild prince of Rio
BackstoryDef.description: Brought to Brazil as a boy when the court fled Napoleon, [PAWN_nameDef] grew up half-wild in Rio de Janeiro, riding horses, chasing adventure and ignoring [PAWN_possessive] tutors.

BackstoryDef.title: soldier king
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] declared Brazil independent and became its first emperor, then came back to fight a civil war for the Portuguese throne, holding out through the long siege of Porto. [PAWN_pronoun] left [PAWN_possessive] heart to the city, and it is still kept there in a jar, in the Lapa church.

BackstoryDef.title: seminary dreamer
BackstoryDef.description: Born in colonial Brazil and educated by the Jesuits, [PAWN_nameDef] spent [PAWN_possessive] lessons staring at the birds outside the window, wondering how they did it.

BackstoryDef.title: flying priest
BackstoryDef.description: In 1709, in front of the king of Portugal, the priest [PAWN_nameDef] floated a small hot-air balloon up towards the ceiling of the palace, seventy years before the Montgolfier brothers, and nearly set the room on fire. [PAWN_pronoun] promised a flying machine shaped like a bird, earned the nickname "the Flying Priest", and ended up fleeing the suspicions of the Inquisition.

BackstoryDef.title: Lagos ship boy
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Lagos, in the Algarve, scrubbing decks and listening to sailors' tales of a sea beyond Cape Bojador that boiled and was full of monsters.

BackstoryDef.title: cape breaker
BackstoryDef.description: For years, every crew sent south turned back at Cape Bojador, terrified of the "Sea of Darkness". In 1434 [PAWN_nameDef] simply kept going, found an ordinary sea on the other side, and came back with a few wild roses to prove it.

BackstoryDef.title: Lisbon street kid
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in the popular neighbourhoods of Lisbon, watching shopkeepers argue with customers and storing up every grumble for later.

BackstoryDef.title: golden-age comic actor
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was the great grumpy face of Portuguese cinema's golden age. As Evaristo, the irascible grocer of "O Pátio das Cantigas", [PAWN_pronoun] was on the receiving end of "Ó Evaristo, tens cá disto?", a line the whole country still quotes eighty years later.

BackstoryDef.title: chorus girl
BackstoryDef.description: Born in a village near Mafra, [PAWN_nameDef] went to Lisbon and joined a theatre chorus at sixteen, determined to be the one everybody looked at.

BackstoryDef.title: film star with a fringe
BackstoryDef.description: Star of "A Aldeia da Roupa Branca" and one of the best-paid actresses of her day, [PAWN_nameDef] wore the same short fringe for most of her life, and to this day Portuguese hairdressers know exactly what a fringe "à Beatriz Costa" means. She later left the stage to travel the world and wrote memoirs with titles like "No Holding My Tongue".

BackstoryDef.title: curious kid
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Aveiro asking everyone questions, and was never satisfied with the first answer.

BackstoryDef.title: eternal reporter
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] covered the Second World War for the BBC from London, joined Portuguese television's staff at the age of seventy-four, and kept reporting until shortly before [PAWN_pronoun] died at ninety-nine, ending every report on the country's absurdities with [PAWN_possessive] immortal "E esta, hein?".

BackstoryDef.title: tailors' daughter
BackstoryDef.description: The daughter of two tailors, [PAWN_nameDef] left school at thirteen to work as a seamstress, entertaining the whole workshop with impressions while the needles flew.

BackstoryDef.title: revue queen
BackstoryDef.description: From a sewing table to the stages of Lisbon's Parque Mayer, [PAWN_nameDef] became one of the great stars of the revue theatre, and later made the whole country laugh in television comedies alongside Camilo de Oliveira.

BackstoryDef.title: Chamusca piano kid
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Chamusca, in the Ribatejo, banging on the family piano until the songs in [PAWN_possessive] head started coming out.

BackstoryDef.title: eccentric rock veteran
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] made a space-age progressive rock album now hailed as a masterpiece, then went to Eurovision with a love song. In the early nineties, furious that radio preferred foreign music, [PAWN_pronoun] posed naked for a magazine with only a gold record to cover [PAWN_objective]self. [PAWN_pronoun] has never once kept an opinion to [PAWN_objective]self.

BackstoryDef.title: Porto music student
BackstoryDef.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up in Porto studying music seriously, playing double bass and jazz long before anyone knew [PAWN_possessive] face. Or [PAWN_possessive] eyes.

BackstoryDef.title: man in dark glasses
BackstoryDef.description: With [PAWN_possessive] band Bandemónio, [PAWN_nameDef] became one of Portugal's biggest singer-songwriters. In all those years in the public eye, almost nobody has ever seen [PAWN_objective] without [PAWN_possessive] dark sunglasses, indoors or out, by day or by night.
